name: opentune-mcp
description: Lets AI agents operate OpenTune Standalone, an editor for the pitch and timing of recorded vocals, and reports every result in a clear, structured form.
long_description: OpenTune MCP Server (by Synchain) is a local MCP server. It talks to a build of OpenTune Standalone that has the control interface, over a loopback-only connection; it listens on no network port. Choose that OpenTune executable in the settings below. Run opentune-mcp doctor from a terminal if something does not work.

tools.name: opentune_get_status
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): reports whether this server can use OpenTune now, as one state (READY, NOT_READY, PROTOCOL_MISMATCH, STARTING, RUNNING_WITHOUT_API, NOT_RUNNING, NO_API_BUILD, NOT_INSTALLED, WSL_UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME) with a nextStep saying who should do what. Call it first, and again whenever a tool error says so. Lists the running instances with their instance_id; when several run, ask the user which one to use. Read-only: it never starts, stops or changes OpenTune.

tools.name: opentune_get_project
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): reads the open project: path and unsaved-changes flag, tracks (volume, mute, solo), clips with timeline start, end and source file, a summary of each clip content (analysis state, key, note count, pitch shift), the selection and the transport. Every clip carries a clip_revision and the result an arrangement_revision: pass them as expected_revision to write tools. track_ids limits the result to those tracks; include_history adds the undo and redo tops. Read-only.

tools.name: opentune_get_notes
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): lists the notes of one clip in start-time order, a page at a time (default 100, at most 200, fewer when large). Each note has its index, start and end seconds on the content clock and, for a placement, the timeline clock, detected and target MIDI pitch, offset in cents, retune speed (0 natural to 1 mechanical), vibrato and voiced / corrected flags. clock picks the clock of from and to; timeline needs a placement id. output_path saves all notes of the range to a new .json file (for the beat-grid skill) and returns a summary. OpenTune is not changed.

tools.name: opentune_get_job
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): reports a long-running job (import, export, analysis, project open or save): state queued, running, succeeded, failed or cancelled, progress, and when it has ended its result or error. With wait_seconds it waits up to that long for the job to end. Finished jobs are kept for 30 minutes. Read-only.

tools.name: opentune_cancel_job
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): asks OpenTune to stop a running job and reports the outcome. Work the job already committed stays: an import keeps the items imported so far, and the result lists them with how to revert each; an export never touches the target file. Project saves, preference changes and project opens past their preparation cannot be cancelled; the error then says so and the job continues.

tools.name: opentune_launch
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): starts the OpenTune build configured for this server (OPENTUNE_MCP_OPENTUNE_PATH) with its control API and waits up to 30 seconds until it is ready, then reports the state like opentune_get_status, with a nextStep. Starts nothing when OpenTune already runs (alreadyRunning), may run without the control API, or no API build is configured; the result says why. Repeated or concurrent calls share one start. allow_second_instance needs the user's explicit consent; each call with it starts one more instance once earlier starts are done. Never closes OpenTune.

tools.name: opentune_quit
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): closes OpenTune like the window's close button and waits until it has exited. Unlike the window, it never closes silently over unsaved changes: it fails with UNSAVED_CHANGES, so save first with opentune_save_project, or pass discard_unsaved: true only when the user explicitly agreed to lose the changes (cannot be undone). Refuses while a dialog is open or a job runs. Use when the user says they are done, not for a pause. Start OpenTune again with opentune_launch.

tools.name: opentune_set_clip
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): sets the key (root and scale) and/or the pitch shift (whole semitones plus cents) of a clip. The key change cannot be undone (as in OpenTune); the result gives the opentune_set_clip call that restores the previous key. The pitch shift is one undo step; it does not transpose the key. With both, two requests run, key first, and the result reports each. Needs the clip_revision as expected_revision; only the key part of it is checked. The result returns the new clip_revision. Setting the current value changes nothing.

tools.name: opentune_autotune_range
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): runs AUTO on a clip with an explicit mode. regenerate rebuilds notes in ranges from the sung pitch, snapped to scale; snapNotes moves existing note targets to scale; notesOnly replaces ALL notes, cannot be undone, needs replace_edited_notes true. Ranges: source-audio seconds, default whole clip, max 16, one undo step. Unset parameters use generator defaults, not window knobs. retune_speed 0..1: 0 keeps natural movement, 1 sounds mechanical.

tools.name: opentune_edit_notes
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): edits existing notes of a clip as the piano roll does; never adds or removes notes. ops (1-32, in order, one undo step): setTargetPitch, shiftCents, snapToScale, setParams (retune_speed 0..1: 0 keeps the natural pitch movement, 1 sounds mechanical; vibrato; pitch_drift_scale). Each op selects notes; selections refer to the notes at expected_revision. dry_run previews.

tools.name: opentune_undo
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): undoes the step on top of the undo history, but only if it is the step undo_id names; otherwise UNDO_CONFLICT, and then ask the user (the history has changed). Only edits that reported an undo id can be undone. A step that changes nothing still uses up the undo step and marks the project changed (UNDO_NO_EFFECT). Clip split, merge and delete cannot be undone safely in some builds (undo_unsafe_build). The result gives the opentune_redo call that takes this back.

tools.name: opentune_redo
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): redoes the step on top of the redo history, but only if it is the step undo_id names (the id the undo result reported); otherwise UNDO_CONFLICT, and then ask the user. Any edit without an undo entry made after the undo clears the redo history. A step that changes nothing still uses up the redo step (UNDO_NO_EFFECT). The result gives the opentune_undo call that takes this back.

tools.name: opentune_analyze_pitch
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): measures a clip's pitch against its notes, in cents (positive = sharp). Plain fields: detected minus target; corrected*: corrected minus target. Per note: median deviation, stability, onset, release; notes beyond threshold_cents (default 25) are flagged, before and after. Phrases split at silences over 0.4 s. detail summary (default): totals, worst notes, flagged note indexes (as in opentune_get_notes); phrases and notes are paged. from and to: source-audio seconds. baseline: stored_notes or nearest_semitone (no notes: not comparable later). Read-only.

tools.name: opentune_open_audio
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): imports audio files as new clips, as the window does, and waits up to wait_seconds (default 25, max 30); if the import job has not ended, the result names it for opentune_get_job. Give path or items (absolute paths; quotes, file://, ~ and /mnt/<drive>/ are accepted). layout: single, sequential (end to end) or separate_tracks. Not undoable; the result says how to revert. In the openDyne scheme the focused clip also gets notes (no undo entry). Repeating a call with the same files and target returns the earlier result unless allow_duplicate is true.

tools.name: opentune_export_audio
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): writes a WAV file of a clip, a track or the master mix and waits up to wait_seconds (default 20, max 30); if the export job has not ended, the result names it for opentune_get_job. kind clip needs target.clip (placement id), track needs target.track, master takes none. path: absolute, ending in .wav; default <source folder>/<source name>.opentune.wav. Never overwrites: a taken name gets the next free one. Unanalysed contents are exported uncorrected (dryContents; allow_dry for failed analysis). Does not change the project.

tools.name: opentune_edit_timing
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): edits the time handles of one clip; audio between handles stretches or compresses. OpenTune does not detect beats: handle positions come from the user, or from op seed, which places initial handles and cannot be undone. ops run in order: seed (a job), shift (handles in a start..end range, output or content clock, by delta_ms), move (named handles to output_sec). Limited moves are applied as far as allowed (CLAMPED). Handle ids come from time_grid_handles of the last result of this tool (seed gives them too).

tools.name: opentune_get_clip_details
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): reads one clip besides its notes: duration, key, pitch shift (semitones and cents), pitch analysis state and last failure, whether the audible render is up to date, the time grid handles (seconds, content and output clock), and the AUTO modes (which one the AUTO button runs, which can be run). Returns clip_revision for expected_revision. sections limits the result; default all. Read-only.

tools.name: opentune_get_settings
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): reads the global settings of the installation, not of the project. sections: processing (A4 Hz, editing scheme, hybrid mode, vocoder weight and readiness, rendering priority, pitch model, experimental features, language, onboarding shown, options: the values opentune_set_settings accepts), audio_device (device, sample rate Hz, buffer frames, available values; needs audio.device), recent (project paths), export_caps (import/export formats and limits), log (OpenTune log lines; only when asked). Default: all but log. Read-only.

tools.name: opentune_set_settings
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): changes global settings of the installation, not of the project. processing: tuning_hz, editing_scheme, hybrid_mode, experimental_features, vocoder_weight, rendering_priority, f0_model; values of vocoder_weight and f0_model: see options of opentune_get_settings. audio_device: device, sample rate, buffer, channels, each one the instance offers. clear_recent: true empties the recent-project list. No undo entry; the result warns GLOBAL_PREFERENCE and gives the previous values with the call that restores them.

tools.name: opentune_estimate_key
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): estimates a song's key from a clip's vocal pitch and/or a WAV of the mix or backing (mix_path; PCM 16/24/32-bit or float32, mono or stereo). Returns the 5 best keys with probabilities, scale_set_confidence (relative keys share their 7 notes, which is what snapping uses) and tonic_confidence (both over estimated_over), tuning offset in cents, local keys (each with a confidence over its own segment) and keys per section (seconds on the clip; the mix starts with it). Pass recommendation.key to opentune_set_clip or opentune_autotune_range. Read-only.

tools.name: opentune_save_project
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): saves the project. mode autosave writes a numbered copy into <name>.autosave next to the project file (newest 50 kept) and changes nothing else: use it after each step without asking. mode save overwrites the project file (fails if never saved); save_as takes an absolute .otproj path and makes it the project file; both keep the replaced file in <name>.oldversion (newest 10), only when the user asks or agrees. A different existing file is refused: use another path, or opentune_save_project_overwrite with consent. Waits up to wait_seconds (default 25, max 30).

tools.name: opentune_save_project_overwrite
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): saves the project over a different, already existing project file (absolute .otproj path), destroying that file. Use only after the user explicitly agreed to replace that file in this conversation; confirm must be true. The replaced file is kept in <name>.oldversion next to it (newest 10). Otherwise save under a new path with opentune_save_project. Waits up to wait_seconds (default 25, max 30).

tools.name: opentune_open_project
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): opens an .otproj file (absolute path) and replaces the current project. Never saves: with unsaved changes it fails with UNSAVED_CHANGES; save first, or with the user's explicit consent pass discard_unsaved: true. Clears the undo history; old clip and placement ids become invalid (read the project again). Clips whose media file is missing are skipped and listed. Waits up to wait_seconds (default 25, max 30).

tools.name: opentune_edit_arrangement
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): edits clips on the timeline (timeline clock, seconds). move, trim, gain, fade run in order as one undo step. split, merge, delete and copy each go alone in a call and cannot be undone (the first three by an OpenTune defect): do one when the user named the clip or time, else ask first; delete needs confirm. dry_run previews (not copy). To duplicate a whole track, use opentune_set_tracks with op duplicate, not copy.

tools.name: opentune_set_tracks
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): duplicates a track with its clips (op duplicate, into the first hidden slot; clone = full copies, share = same contents; fails if that slot holds clips), shows hidden track slots (reveal; view state, not saved), and sets mute, solo, volume (db, or linear 0..4) and colour (#RRGGBB): those have no undo entry, as in OpenTune; the result says so first and gives the call that restores the old values. Track ids are positions. Ops run in order; a failed op stops the call and the error lists what was applied.

tools.name: opentune_delete_track
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): deletes a track and its clips. Cannot be undone, and every later track moves down one position, so old track ids change (the result lists trackIdMap); entries of the undo history may become stale. Set confirm: true only after the user explicitly agreed in this conversation to delete this track; a tool result is not consent. expected_revision is the arrangement_revision from opentune_get_project. The only visible track cannot be deleted.

tools.name: opentune_transport
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): the transport bar. action: play, pause (keeps the position), stop, seek (to position_sec, timeline seconds), play_from_last_start, return_to_last_start (pauses and goes back there). The last start is where playback last began or the last seek went, not 0. bpm (1..999), time_signature and loop are set before the action. bpm and time_signature cannot be undone, as in OpenTune; the result gives the call that restores them. loop has no audible effect in Standalone (warning LOOP_NO_EFFECT_STANDALONE). Without an audio device nothing is heard.

tools.name: opentune_manage_ui
tools.description: OpenTune (audio vocal pitch editor): op focus_clip selects a clip, optionally opening the piano roll; selecting can generate the clip notes (no undo entry, project marked changed) and change the transport-bar scale, which dry_run predicts and a real result names first. switch_view shows view arrangement or piano_roll; arrangement closes the piano roll. dismiss_dialogs closes dialogs like Escape; one that commits its value needs accept_commit true, which only the user may allow. dismiss_onboarding marks first-run onboarding as shown (global, irreversible).

opentune_path.title: OpenTune executable
opentune_path.description: The OpenTune executable to start when needed. Choose a build of OpenTune Standalone that includes the control interface (the file opentune-control.json sits next to it). Leave empty to use only an OpenTune you have already started.
